title: Union cover variant (open problem)
statement_text: For every graph $H$, and all $\varepsilon > 0$, there is an integer $N$ such that for every $H$-free graph $G$, $V(G)$ is the union of at most $N$ $\varepsilon$-restricted subsets (not necessarily pairwise disjoint).
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple, and $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$. A set $X\subseteq V(G)$ is $\varepsilon$-restricted if one of $G[X]$, $\overline{G}[X]$ has maximum degree at most $\varepsilon|X|$, and weakly $\varepsilon$-restricted if one of them has at most $\varepsilon|X|^2$ edges. Rödl's theorem says that every $H$-free graph has a (weakly) $\varepsilon$-restricted set of linear size, and applying it repeatedly easily shows that $V(G)$ can be partitioned into a bounded number of weakly $\varepsilon$-restricted subsets. The main theorem of the paper is the much harder statement that for every $H$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is $N$ such that the vertex set of every $H$-free graph can be partitioned into at most $N$ $\varepsilon$-restricted subsets; some parts must sometimes have size at most two (e.g. in a large star). The union-cover statement is described as midway between these two results. The authors remark that it does not seem easy to prove directly and, as far as they know, does not imply their partition theorem. Since a partition is in particular a covering by not necessarily disjoint sets, the statement follows from the partition theorem proved in the paper; it is not presented as an open problem.
notes: Stated as a passing remark without a labelled environment; the authors signal it is open and non-trivial but do not explicitly phrase it as a conjecture or question.
